Snowdonia: A Scenic Motorcycle Route Guide

Snowdonia National Park contains some of Britain's most exciting motorcycle roads. Mountain passes climb through ancient glacial valleys, lakeside roads wind beneath towering crags, and the whole area is compact enough to ride in a long weekend. Here's a two-day route hitting the highlights.

Day 1: The Passes (100 miles)

Start from Betws-y-Coed and head west on the A5 to Capel Curig, then climb the dramatic Llanberis Pass (A4086) — a narrow road beneath the towering crags of Snowdon's east face. Descend through Llanberis and loop south via Caernarfon to the Nantlle Valley. Continue through the Aberglaslyn Pass and over the Crimea Pass to return to Betws-y-Coed.

  • Key roads: Llanberis Pass (A4086), A498 through Beddgelert, A470 through the Crimea Pass
  • Key stops: Pen-y-Pass summit viewpoint, Beddgelert village, Swallow Falls near Betws-y-Coed

Day 2: The Lakes and Coast (110 miles)

Head south from Betws-y-Coed through the Migneint moorland to Dolgellau, then ride the spectacular Cross Foxes road (A487) and continue to Cadair Idris. Loop west to the coast at Barmouth, then north along the coast via Harlech Castle to Portmeirion, and back inland through the Vale of Ffestiniog.

  • Key roads: A470 south through Migneint, A493 coastal road, A487 via Harlech
  • Key stops: Cadair Idris viewpoint, Harlech Castle, Portmeirion village, Barmouth bridge
Snowdonia's roads are technical — narrow, twisty, and often slippery with mountain drainage. They reward smooth riding and moderate speed rather than flat-out speed. Take it steady and you'll enjoy every bend.

When to Visit

  • Best months: May, June, and September offer the best balance of weather and quiet roads.
  • Summer holidays: July and August bring heavy tourist traffic to the most popular passes. Start early.
  • Autumn: October brings stunning colours in the oak woodlands and fewer crowds.

Practical Tips

  • Fuel stations in Betws-y-Coed, Dolgellau, and Porthmadog. Mid-route options are limited.
  • The A4086 Llanberis Pass can be very busy — ride it early morning for the best experience.
  • Watch for cyclists — Snowdonia is hugely popular with road cyclists and mountain bikers.

Where to Stay and Eat

Betws-y-Coed is the traditional base for Snowdonia motorcycle touring, with good fuel stations, accommodation ranging from campsites to comfortable hotels, and several excellent restaurants. Beddgelert is quieter and arguably prettier — one of Wales's most charming villages nestled where two rivers meet beneath wooded hills. Dolgellau at the southern end of the park gives access to Cadair Idris and the stunning Mawddach Estuary trail. All three towns have biker-friendly B&Bs and nearby campsites that welcome motorcycle tourers.

For food, the Ty Gwyn Hotel in Betws-y-Coed serves excellent Welsh lamb that rivals anything in the country. The fish and chips at The Big Rock Café in Porthmadog are legendary among touring riders visiting North Wales. The national park visitor centres at Betws-y-Coed and Beddgelert provide detailed maps, current weather updates, and reliable local road condition information that is invaluable for planning your daily routes through the mountain passes.
keyTakeaways: This two-day route from Betws-y-Coed splits into a passes day and a lakes-and-coast day, each around 100 to 110 miles.
Day 1 climbs the Llanberis Pass (A4086) beneath Snowdon's east face and loops via Beddgelert and the Crimea Pass.
Day 2 runs south through the Migneint to Dolgellau, Cadair Idris, Harlech Castle and Portmeirion.
Snowdonia's roads are narrow, twisty and often slippery with mountain drainage, rewarding smooth riding over speed.

faq.q: How busy does the Llanberis Pass get?
faq.a: The A4086 Llanberis Pass can be very busy, especially in July and August and on weekends, with heavy tourist traffic to Pen-y-Pass and Snowdon. Ride it early in the morning for the best experience, when the road is quieter and the light on Snowdon's crags is at its most dramatic. Watch for road cyclists too, as Snowdonia is hugely popular with them.

faq.q: What is the riding like underfoot?
faq.a: Snowdonia's roads are technical: narrow, twisty and often slippery with mountain drainage running across the surface. They reward smooth, moderate riding rather than flat-out speed. Take the bends steadily, especially in the wet, and you will enjoy every mile. The passes such as Llanberis and the Crimea Pass demand particular care on their tighter, exposed sections.

May, June and September offer the best balance of weather and quiet roads. July and August bring heavy tourist traffic to the most popular passes, so start early if you ride then. October brings stunning colours in the oak woodlands and fewer crowds. Whenever you go, pack waterproofs, as the western mountains catch a lot of rain.

faq.q: Where can I refuel and stay?
faq.a: Fuel stations are in Betws-y-Coed, Dolgellau and Porthmadog, with limited options mid-route, so top up in these towns. Betws-y-Coed is the traditional touring base with good facilities. Beddgelert is quieter and arguably prettier, while Dolgellau at the southern end gives access to Cadair Idris and the Mawddach Estuary. All three have biker-friendly B&Bs and nearby campsites.
